requirement.title: Recurring appointment sequence cadence configurations
requirement.description: The Recurring Appointment Sequence Cadence Configurations module enables healthcare schedulers and clinical personnel to set up automated, repeating appointment series for patients requiring long-term care management, physical therapy, or chronic condition follow-ups. The module ensures adherence to patient care plans while maintaining system performance and avoiding schedule overlaps.
acceptance_criteria: Schedulers can set custom recurring appointment intervals including weekly, bi-weekly, and monthly cadences.
The system must enforce a hard limit of max 52 recurring appointment occurrences per sequence.
Automated conflict resolution must flag overlapping provider time slots during sequence generation.
Sequence cadence modifications automatically update all remaining future uncompleted visits.
System generates automated SMS and email reminders 48 hours prior to each recurring appointment instance.
Audit logs must record all cadence modifications with user ID, timestamp, and previous schedule parameters.

requirement.title: Provider out-of-office blockouts with automated patient re-assignment
requirement.description: The Provider Out-Of-Office (OOO) Blockouts module allows clinical providers to schedule planned or unplanned absences. When a blockout is established, the platform automatically identifies affected patient appointments, attempts automated re-assignment to an available on-call provider within the same clinical specialty, and routes unassigned visits to a pending queue while notifying impacted patients.
acceptance_criteria: Providers can schedule out-of-office blockout time frames across single or multi-day periods.
The system must automatically identify all patient appointments impacted by an out-of-office blockout.
Impacted patient appointments must be automatically re-assigned to an available on-call provider within the same specialty.
If no on-call provider is available, impacted appointments are routed to the unassigned pending queue.
Re-assigned patients must receive automated notification of provider change via SMS within 15 minutes.
All blockout creations and re-assignments must generate complete audit logs.

requirement.title: Multi-provider calendar synchronization via CalDAV protocols
requirement.description: This requirement defines the functionality for synchronizing external provider calendars with the core EHR platform using standardized CalDAV protocols. The objective is to establish bi-directional availability sync across external scheduling platforms to streamline multi-provider workflows.
acceptance_criteria: System must synchronize appointments across multiple provider external calendars using CalDAV standard protocols.
Sync cycles must execute automatically every 15 minutes or upon manual user trigger.
Conflicts between internal EHR schedules and external CalDAV entries must flag status as "Conflict Pending Review" without overwriting existing patient appointments.
Access credentials for external CalDAV servers must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption.
Detailed sync activity logs containing provider ID, timestamp, and status must be recorded in the system audit trail.
Sync failures due to network timeouts or invalid credentials must generate a system notification to the clinic administrator.

requirement.title: Real-time slot reservation locking to prevent double-booking
requirement.description: This requirement specifies the implementation of real-time reservation locks on patient scheduling slots to eliminate concurrent booking race conditions and prevent double-booking across patient portals and staff scheduling interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: System must place a temporary 10-minute reservation lock on an appointment time slot as soon as a patient begins booking.
Locked appointment slots must display as "Held" to other concurrent users in real time via WebSocket updates.

requirement.title: Reach Manual Member Alert Inactivation and Audit Trail
requirement.description: The Reach SaaS platform provides care managers and coordinators with real-time operational alerts regarding patient care gaps, risk escalations, and task follow-ups. This requirement defines the workflow for manually inactivating active member alerts, capturing audit trails, enforcing supervisory oversight for reactivations, and suppressing automated outreach upon alert inactivation.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized care coordinators can manually inactivate active member alerts from the Reach portal dashboard.
The system must record every inactivation event in the audit log, capturing user ID, timestamp, and inactivation reason.
Inactivated alerts must be immediately removed from the active alert queue and moved to the archived alerts tab.
Re-activating an inactivated alert requires explicit supervisor role approval and a justification entry.
Inactivating an alert must automatically suspend pending automated SMS notifications for that specific alert.
The platform must support bulk inactivation for up to 250 member alerts simultaneously via CSV upload.

requirement.title: Outbound Fax Dispatch to Assigned Care Team Provider
requirement.description: The Outbound Fax Dispatch engine facilitates secure, automated transmission of clinical care plans, transition of care summaries, and authorization requests directly to the verified fax numbers of assigned primary care providers (PCPs) within the care team panel.
acceptance_criteria: System shall automatically route outbound clinical faxes to the assigned primary care provider's verified fax number.
If primary care provider fax delivery fails, system shall attempt retry up to 3 times at 5-minute intervals.
System shall generate a transmission audit record containing timestamp, recipient fax number, page count, and status.
If all retries fail, the outbound fax shall be routed to the central unassigned fax review queue.

System administrators can manually unlock locked sessions prior to timer expiration via the Security Admin Portal.

requirement.title: Member Risk Score Recalculation on Diagnosis Code Update
requirement.description: This document specifies the operational and technical requirements for automatically triggering, calculating, and auditing Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) risk score adjustments within the Reach Healthcare Platform whenever a member's diagnosis records are updated.
acceptance_criteria: The system must automatically trigger a recalculation of a member's Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) risk score whenever an ICD-10 diagnosis code is added, updated, or deleted in the member record.
Risk score recalculations must complete within 30 seconds of the diagnosis change submission.
If an updated diagnosis code increases the member's risk category, an automated risk stratification alert must be logged in the member timeline.
Historical risk scores and their associated calculation timestamps must be retained without overwriting existing records.
Invalid or deprecated ICD-10 codes must reject the recalculation request and flag an error in the ingestion queue.
Recalculation logs must record the triggering user or source API, previous score, updated score, and effective date.

requirement.title: Provider Network Credentialing and Enrollment Status Sync
requirement.description: This document outlines the business rules and synchronization specifications between external credentialing verification databases (such as CAQH ProView) and the Reach platform's provider directory and enrollment management system.
acceptance_criteria: The system must synchronize provider credentialing status changes from the CAQH data bridge every 24 hours.
Expired provider licenses must automatically set the provider network enrollment status to "Suspended-Pending-Review".
Primary source verification (PSV) completion must update the credentialing status to "Approved" and send an email notification to the provider portal user.
Provider credentialing sync attempts must log the transaction status, timestamp, and source payload ID in the integration audit ledger.
Failed synchronization attempts must trigger an automated retry after 15 minutes up to a maximum of 3 attempts before raising an IT operational ticket.

requirement.title: Prior Authorization Denial Appeal Tracking and Resolution
requirement.description: This requirement defines the functionality for managing, tracking, and resolving appeals resulting from prior authorization denials within the health plan's care management ecosystem. It establishes automated workflow tracking, document management, and communication mechanisms to ensure compliance with regulatory notification timelines.
acceptance_criteria: System must log initial prior authorization denial details, including denial code, date, and clinical rationale.
Users can initiate a 1st-level or 2nd-level appeal workflow with auto-populated member and denial context.
The platform must track appeal submission deadlines and alert care managers 5 days prior to expiration.
Clinical staff can upload and attach supporting medical documentation directly to the active appeal file.
The system must record outcome decisions (Upheld, Overturned, Partial Approval) with resolution timestamps.
Automated notification must be sent to the prescribing provider upon final appeal resolution.

requirement.title: Medication Adherence Monitoring and Pharmacy Outreach Trigger
requirement.description: This business specification details the automated compliance monitoring for chronic disease medication regimes. The system analyzes pharmacy claims data to identify non-adherent members based on Proportion of Days Covered (PDC) calculations and triggers proactive pharmacy intervention tasks.
acceptance_criteria: The system must calculate Proportion of Days Covered (PDC) metrics nightly for targeted chronic medication classes.
Members falling below an 80% PDC threshold must be automatically flagged as non-adherent.
The system must generate an automated pharmacy outreach trigger task when a member is flagged as non-adherent.
Clinical users can document outreach attempts, member-reported barriers, and resolution statuses in the intervention log.
The platform must suppress new outreach triggers for 30 days once an outreach task is marked completed or in-progress.
